item.title: South Korea: Samsung faces an HBM base die crunch as internal demand is seen doubling to 30,000 wafers a month
item.description: TrendForce reported on 25 November, citing industry sources, that Samsung's memory division will need roughly 30,000 4nm-equivalent base die wafers a month in 2027, about double this year, and that 4nm base die output is confined to select foundry lines at Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek. Samsung reportedly plans to convert its Giheung R&D line to 4nm base die, dedicate part of Pyeongtaek P5 to base die, and tentatively earmark Taylor P2 in Texas for HBM5 base dies for AMD and Nvidia; it is also said to be developing an HBM4E custom base die for Meta on its 2nm process. Hankyung reports Samsung targets doubling HBM4/HBM4E output in 2027, with HBM wafer input rising from 180,000 to 250,000 a month. Caveat: unconfirmed by Samsung. Country conversion: custom HBM is pulling Korean foundry capacity, and part of it to Texas, into the AI memory chain. [Signal 36, Single-source, via TrendForce, 25 Nov 2026, citing Seoul Economic Daily, Maeil Business, The Bell, Hankyung] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Dell books $60.2 billion of AI server orders and ends Q3 with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog
item.description: Dell Technologies reported fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on 24 November: revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103 per cent year on year, with AI-optimized server revenue of $22.0 billion, up 291 per cent, and Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue of $42.0 billion. Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders in the quarter and ended with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog, which COO Jeff Clarke said was vetted for customer quality and access to capital, land and power. Full-year guidance rose to $202.0 billion of revenue (from $192.0 billion) and $78.0 billion of AI-optimized server revenue (from $74.0 billion). Caveat: backlog is not revenue, and Dell shares fell with chip stocks on 25 November as AI spending and financing concerns resurfaced. Country conversion: US AI factory demand is still converting into firm server orders at OEM level, even as OEMs reprice contracts for memory inflation. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via Dell Technologies Q3 FY27 press release, 24 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Finland: XTX Markets opens its first 22.5 MW Kajaani data centre and warns grid expropriation delays threaten more investment
item.description: XTX Markets said on 24 November that the first data centre on its 193-hectare Kajaani campus is open, with 22.5 MW of IT capacity and 15,000 square metres of floor space; the second facility is due in 2027. The firm has invested over EUR 400 million, mostly with Finnish contractors, and says it has ambitions to invest billions more. Power and grid connections are secured for the first two facilities, but COO Mike Irwin said expropriation permits for grid development that once took months now take years, leaving power for the third facility (due mid-2028) and later annual builds uncertain. Caveat: this is the company's own account of the permitting dispute; no government response was published. Country conversion: Finland is converting private AI compute into domestic capacity, but grid-line permitting is now the gating item. [Signal 38, Confirmed, via XTX Markets press release, 24 Nov 2026; DCD; Yle] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Estonia: Elering says data centre connection requests reach 3.3 GW, nearly twice national peak demand
item.description: Estonian transmission operator Elering told ERR on 24 November that data centre connection requests have reached 3,300 MW, nearly twice Estonia's peak electricity demand. It has signed connection agreements for 600 MW and has active offers for a further 1,300 MW, and board member Reigo Kebja said Elering is close to the point where it cannot issue new connection offers. Economy Minister Erkki Keldo said he will discuss with developers whether projects should bring new domestic generation or pay additional taxes; Finland is already considering a generation requirement. Only one major site operates today (Greenergy, Hüüru, drawing about 2 MW, planned to 200 MW by early 2028, hosting a Nebius AI factory). Caveat: many applications may never be built. Country conversion: Baltic grid headroom, not demand, is now the limit on AI load in Estonia. [Signal 36, Single-source, via ERR News, 24 Nov 2026 (Elering)] More: https://compute.world/wire

Google told DCD that no final decision has been made on Ozans or any other site and that these are exploratory long-term planning, not active parallel projects; the local mayor said the plan was on hold and the landowner has opposed a sale. item.title: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand: BIS adds seven Megaspeed-linked firms to the Entity List
item.description: The Bureau of Industry and Security filed a final rule for public inspection on 23 November (FR Doc 2026-23999, publication 25 November) adding seven entities to the Entity List for significant risk of diverting advanced computing commodities: Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd., Swiftdata Pte. Ltd. and Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) in Singapore; Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, MSFusion Sdn. Bhd. and PT Megaspeed International under Malaysia; and Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. A licence is required for all items subject to the EAR, reviewed under a presumption of denial; goods already en route may proceed if delivered within 30 days. Malaysia's MITI said on 24 November that MIDA will tell all data centre operators not to host, lease space to or serve the listed entities. Caveat: the rule gives no detail of the alleged diversion; Megaspeed has previously denied wrongdoing. Country conversion: the first named enforcement under the new remote-access regime lands on Southeast Asian neocloud capacity, a day after Nvidia reinstated Huang. [Signal 54, Confirmed, via BIS final rule, Federal Register public inspection, 23 Nov 2026; Malaysia MITI, 24 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

Caveat: the application says no final site decision has been made, county records show TSMC has not bought the land, and officials say Sherman is still under review. item.title: US: Nvidia board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, citing input from senior US government officials
item.description: Nvidia announced on 23 November that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, eleven days after he resigned on 12 November. The board said it received input from senior levels of the US government and, on that basis, is confident the reinstatement poses no national security risk. Harvey Jones stays as chair; Colette Kress returns to CFO only. The independent-director investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort continues, a new National Security and Export Control Committee is retaining counsel, and Nvidia is searching for a Chief Compliance Officer. Caveat: AP reports the board had rejected Huang's offer to return days earlier. Country conversion: Washington now has a visible hand in the governance of the dominant accelerator vendor, ahead of Huang's 1 December House interviews. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via Nvidia newsroom, 23 Nov 2026; AP; The Verge, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

Financing runs through its $5 billion Macquarie equity programme then project finance; delivery is expected to begin in the first half of 2028. Caveat: site and tenant not named. item.title: Spain: data centre decree in force, with 80 per cent hourly-matched new renewables and curtailment duties
item.description: Royal Decree 1032/2026, approved by the Council of Ministers on 20 November and published in the BOE on 21 November, took effect on 22 November. It applies to data centres that have sought or will seek grid access and connection permits. They must cover 80 per cent of consumption with new renewable supply through self-consumption or PPAs, matched hourly, with an optional transition of 60 per cent, 70 per cent from 2029 and 80 per cent from 2032, and a compensation charge (6 euros per MWh at 60 to 80 per cent annual coverage) for shortfalls. Sites must also join automatic power-reduction schemes and can be disconnected to protect the system; water and PUE limits apply, and Article 5 sets data-location rules for high-category public systems. Minister Aagesen said that without the rule bills could rise by up to 5 billion euros. Caveat: operators contested feasibility; grid-queue effects are not yet visible. Country conversion: Spain now prices grid access for AI load in renewables and flexibility. [Signal 44, Confirmed, via BOE, 21 Nov 2026; MITECO, 20 Nov 2026; DCD, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Apollo and Goldman price about $44 billion of notes to buy Vera Rubin GPUs for SpaceX

Proceeds buy Nvidia Vera Rubin systems for SpaceX's terrestrial compute build; lease schedules start on delivery in the first half of 2027. IFR reports the public tranches price at 7.66 to 8.36 per cent, with the largest ($25.2 billion senior secured, due April 2033) at 8.259 per cent. Caveat: tranche detail is from IFR, not the press release. Country conversion: US compute is now financed as a leased asset class at high-yield coupons, and the collateral is next-generation Nvidia silicon. [Signal 48, Confirmed, via Apollo / Goldman Sachs press release, 20 Nov 2026; IFR; DCD, 23 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Trump threatens to block or tax US companies that build data centres abroad
item.description: At a White House press conference on 20 November, President Trump said: "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," then added that if they do, "we're going to put a tremendous tax on them." He said he had not yet raised the idea with his staff and named China and Finland in his remarks. No rate, scope, start date or legal authority was given, and no presidential action or Federal Register rule had been published as of 21 November. Caveat: Congress holds the taxing power and the Supreme Court ruled in February 2026 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs, so this is a stated intention, not policy. Country conversion: a credible penalty would tilt hyperscaler capex toward US sites and raise the political price of offshore campuses that host US-controlled silicon, at the same time as the BIS remote-access rule tightens Southeast Asia. [Signal 52, Corroborated, via CNBC, 20 Nov 2026; AP; Axios, 20 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Taiwan: TSMC holds some shipments to Chinese and non-Chinese designers while it reviews the BIS 16nm and 14nm presumption
item.description: Nikkei Asia reported on 20 November that TSMC has put several shipments to Chinese and non-Chinese chip designers on hold while it checks compliance with the BIS interim final rule that took effect 19 November. Under the rule, foundries and OSATs must presume chips made on 16nm, 14nm or more advanced nodes are controlled advanced-computing chips unless the designer supplies certified Total Processing Performance or performance-density documentation; fewer than 30 billion transistors and no HBM is not by itself proof of exemption. Industry executives told Nikkei the scope reaches smartphone, automotive and consumer chips. Caveat: single outlet, TSMC has not commented publicly and the volume held is not disclosed. Country conversion: the US is pushing compliance onto Taiwan's foundry gate, so every designer on a modern node now needs paperwork before wafers ship. [Signal 46, Single-source, via Nikkei Asia, 20 Nov 2026; Tom's Hardware, 22 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: Southeast Asia: at least two Nvidia server partners halt shipments to the region after the BIS licence rule
item.description: Nikkei Asia reported from Taipei on 20 November that at least two Nvidia server partners have stopped shipping to Southeast Asian customers. One unnamed maker halted all shipments to the region from 20 November and stopped taking orders from new regional clients while it gathers customer information for licence applications; another paused on legal advice although its servers were compliant. A third keeps shipping but will seek licences for orders placed after 19 November and is shifting focus to Japan and South Korea. Suppliers fear the hit falls on clusters in Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore and Indonesia. Caveat: companies unnamed; Reuters relayed the Nikkei report. Country conversion: the BIS remote-access rule is already converting into delivery delays and inventory risk for the region's neocloud build. [Signal 48, Single-source, via Nikkei Asia, 20 Nov 2026; Reuters via Lianhe Zaobao, 22 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Army opens nine installations to 25-year leases for power generation paired with data centres
item.description: The Army's Strategic Capital Initiative released RFP DACA27-1-27-0015900 (dated 19 November, announced 20 November) seeking enhanced-use lease proposals for commercial power generation, optionally paired with data centres, at Fort Bragg, Blue Grass Army Depot, Pine Bluff Arsenal, Fort Rucker, Fort Hood, Fort McCoy, Sierra Army Depot, Tooele Army Depot and Joint Base Lewis-McChord. Data-centre-only bids are excluded; power must reach the installation within one hour of a grid outage for at least 14 days, with a preference for up to 90 days. The initial term is 25 years; site tours run 30 November to 17 December and proposals are due 18 January 2027. Caveat: parcels vary widely and some (Tooele) carry groundwater contamination. Country conversion: US federal land is being offered to AI builders on condition they bring their own generation. [Signal 40, Confirmed, via US Army SCI RFP DACA27-1-27-0015900 (SAM.gov); Holland & Knight, 23 Nov 2026; DCD] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: US: Senate passes BAAJA 62 to 33, making data centres pay embedded and incremental grid costs
item.description: The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 by 62 to 33 on 19 November; 14 Democrats and one independent joined most Republicans. Section 2107 would direct FERC, within 270 days of enactment, to revise its 1994 transmission pricing policy so computational loads pay both embedded and incremental expansion costs, and sets ratepayer protections for covered loads of 20 MW or more (including multi-site loads under common control and phased projects expected to reach 20 MW). It also widens FERC permitting authority for interstate transmission and shortens federal environmental reviews. Caveat: the House passed a narrower version last year; the bill is not law. Country conversion: if enacted, US grid cost for large AI campuses moves from the ratebase onto the tenant, raising delivered cost per MW in tight markets such as PJM. [Signal 54, Confirmed, via DCD, 19 Nov 2026; AP; NPR, 20 Nov 2026; USA Today; Foley Hoag bill analysis] More: https://compute.world/wire

item.title: China: House committee discloses US approvals for 879,868 H200 and MI325X chips to Chinese buyers, none shipped as of May

Every approval in the released table is marked approved, not shipped. Nearly all Nvidia applications list Maginfra, Beijing New Matrix, ZTE Kangxun or Lenovo as installers, and every application rated diversion risk low. Caveat: data is six months old; shipments since May are not disclosed. Country conversion: China's licensed import pipeline for frontier US silicon is large on paper and politically exposed, with the same day's AMD short report and California subpoena of Nvidia adding pressure. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via House Foreign Affairs Committee ECRA disclosure, 19 Nov 2026; CNBC; The Register, 20 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire
